tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to approved orders and receipts, then record them in AFAS.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives in Outlook or an agency portal.
steps: Find the order, agreed prices and evidence that goods or services were received.
Compare supplier, quantities, rates, VAT and totals.
Ask the site or budget owner about missing approvals or differences.
Enter the invoice and supporting references in AFAS.
drudgery: Comparing agency invoices with approved hours
today.time_sinks: Missing order references, scattered receipt evidence and repeated follow-up across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

lenses.faster: Extract invoice fields once and compare them automatically with approved orders and receipts. Manual work concentrates on differences and missing evidence.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice arrival starts validation, duplicate checks and matching. Only invoices within approved rules proceed automatically to accounting.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours and contracted rates, with a breakdown by site. Identify recurring overcharges before they become a month-end problem.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and document hunting. Keep the supplier conversations and investigations where the bookkeeper can resolve a real problem.
lenses.options: For a mismatch, present supported choices such as requesting a credit, correcting a reference or seeking receipt confirmation. Show the evidence and accounting effect of each.
lenses.altitude: Own matching rules, exception categories and supplier data quality across the three sites.
reach: Help procurement identify suppliers that repeatedly invoice outside agreed terms.
Give the Controller an evidence-backed list of received services awaiting invoices.

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a plausible match conceals a service dispute, unusual supplier behaviour or an unauthorised purchase.
tasks.pattern_why: A model can extract fields from varied documents; deterministic checks must establish duplicates, arithmetic, order matches and posting eligibility.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice enters the controlled invoice inbox or an authorised portal import.
steps: Capture the original document and extract fields with source references.
Validate supplier identity, duplicate indicators, arithmetic and required VAT information.
Match against approved orders, receipt evidence or approved agency hours using configured tolerances.
Record eligible invoices through a supported AFAS route and send exceptions to the responsible owner.
Track resolution and retain the evidence behind each match.
in_practice.human_gate: Finance approves rules and tolerances before activation; bookkeepers resolve exceptions. Budget approval remains required, and payment release follows a separate approval process.
systems: Proposed invoice extraction and matching service
data_needed: Supplier master and approved supplier identifiers
Orders, receipt confirmations and approval status
Approved agency hours and effective rate agreements
VAT rules, tolerances and posting permissions
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS document and transaction references plus a restricted matching log recording sources, rule versions, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports purchase invoice accounting; this does not establish that Noordhaven has automated order and receipt matching configured.
Document extraction followed by rule-based matching is technically plausible; the proposed integration and savings require a pilot.

risks: An incorrect match can hide a duplicate, overcharge or missing receipt.
Staffing agency rates may depend on dates, shifts and contract conditions that are absent from the invoice.
Changed bank details must not be accepted through invoice extraction; independently verify supplier master changes.
Invoices can contain personal data, requiring restricted access and approved processing arrangements under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: What proportion of invoices has an approved order and reliable receipt evidence before arrival?
Can AFAS expose the necessary records and accept controlled invoice entries through supported interfaces?
Do all three agencies provide invoice lines, approved hours and effective rate agreements in a usable format?
On a representative sample, how many incorrect matches and manual exceptions remain under proposed tolerances?

tasks.short: Calculate debits, credits and account totals in AFAS and supporting spreadsheets.

today.trigger: A transaction batch, adjustment or account schedule needs calculation.
steps: Collect approved transaction data and relevant account balances.
Calculate amounts and debit or credit movements in AFAS or Excel.
Check that entries balance and agree with supporting schedules.
Record the entries and retain the calculation.
today.time_sinks: Inconsistent spreadsheet layouts, broken formulas and manual checks that duplicate calculations already performed by AFAS.

lenses.faster: Use approved calculation rules and controlled imports so totals and balancing checks run automatically. Remove duplicate spreadsheet arithmetic wherever AFAS already performs it.
lenses.autonomous: An approved source batch triggers calculation, validation and eligible routine entries. Unbalanced or out-of-policy batches stop before posting.
lenses.ambitious: Validate every batch at line level and detect unusual signs, amounts and account combinations before close.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive arithmetic and formula repair. Leave the person to explain unusual movements and improve the controls.
lenses.options: Compare permitted rounding or allocation methods before Finance selects a policy. Production runs use the approved method consistently.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a small library of tested calculation rules and monitor where manual adjustments still occur.
reach: Maintain recurring calculation schedules for the Accountant.
Provide the Controller with earlier account movement checks.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when balanced arithmetic still represents the wrong economic event or accounting treatment.
tasks.pattern_why: Debit and credit arithmetic, rounding and balancing have explicit rules and checkable outputs. A language model is unnecessary in the production calculation path.

in_practice.trigger: An approved transaction batch becomes available.
steps: Read source amounts and the current approved calculation rules.
Calculate debit and credit lines using fixed decimal precision and explicit rounding.
Check balancing, account validity, period status and source control totals.
Post eligible routine batches through a supported AFAS route; hold failures for review.
Reconcile accepted entries to the source batch and archive the calculation.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves calculation rules and eligible posting types. Bookkeepers resolve failures; unusual adjustments require approval before posting.
systems: Proposed controlled calculation and import workflow
data_needed: Chart of accounts and valid dimensions
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS batch references and a restricted calculation register containing input totals, rule versions, validation results and posting receipts.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit provides general ledger accounting with debit and credit entries.
Controlled calculations and balanced batch validation can be implemented without a model at runtime; Noordhaven's remaining manual work is unmeasured.

risks: Incorrect rules can produce balanced but wrong entries at scale.
Duplicate imports can repeat otherwise valid transactions.
Spreadsheet calculations may contain undocumented accounting judgements.
Most arithmetic may already be automated, leaving little incremental saving.
research_questions: Which calculations still require manual work beyond standard AFAS functions?
Can recurring schedules be expressed as approved rules without hidden judgement?
How will retries prevent duplicate postings and reconcile partial batch failures?
Does a pilot reduce handling time without increasing correction journals or audit findings?

tasks.short: Code transactions to the right accounts and sites, then keep the financial records complete.

today.trigger: An invoice, credit, receipt or adjustment needs classification.
steps: Read the source document and identify the business purpose.
Select the general ledger account, site, cost centre and VAT treatment.
Check supporting evidence and obtain clarification where needed.
Record the transaction and review the resulting account summary.
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous descriptions, inconsistent supplier coding and uncertainty about which site incurred the cost.

lenses.faster: Reuse approved mappings for recurring transactions and suggest coding for unfamiliar descriptions. Show the supporting document beside the proposed entry.
lenses.autonomous: Recognised recurring transactions follow approved coding rules. New or ambiguous transactions arrive as drafts for review.
lenses.ambitious: Apply consistent site and cost coding throughout the month so the forecast starts from cleaner actuals.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive account lookups. Keep the judgement involved in understanding a new expense and improving its description.
lenses.options: For ambiguous costs, show a few supported account choices and explain their effect on site reporting and period expense.
lenses.altitude: Become the owner of coding quality, recurring mappings and the feedback that improves them.
reach: Help FP&A maintain reliable site cost categories.
Help the Accountant identify possible accruals, prepayments and fixed assets.

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting business substance, especially when costs cross periods, sites or accounting categories.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured descriptions can support coding suggestions, but approved mappings and accounting validations must control what reaches the ledger.

in_practice.trigger: A validated transaction is ready for coding.
steps: Read the document, supplier record and permitted coding dimensions.
Apply an approved recurring mapping or generate a source-backed coding suggestion.
Check account combinations, VAT requirements, period and site consistency.
Present the proposed entry and alternatives to the bookkeeper.
Post the approved coding and record corrections for controlled mapping review.
in_practice.human_gate: A bookkeeper approves proposed coding before posting. The Accountant decides material accrual, capitalisation and unusual VAT treatments.
data_needed: Chart of accounts, sites and cost centres
Source documents and approved supplier records
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS entry history and a restricted coding log with the suggestion, evidence, reviewer decision and mapping version.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports financial transaction recording and general ledger reporting.
A model can suggest structured coding from descriptions and supplied policies, but coding quality needs validation against reviewed examples.

risks: Historical mistakes may be repeated as apparently established practice.
Supplier identity alone may not determine the correct account or VAT treatment.
Incorrect site coding can distort forecasts while leaving the ledger balanced.
Document text must be treated as data and must not override workflow instructions or permissions.
research_questions: What share of transactions follows a stable, approved coding pattern?
How accurate are existing historical account and site labels?
Which coding decisions require Accountant approval rather than bookkeeper approval?
Does the pilot reduce review time while preserving account, site and VAT accuracy?

tasks.short: Move approved journal details into AFAS and check that every line arrived correctly.

today.trigger: A separate journal or spreadsheet is ready for ledger transfer.
steps: Collect the approved journal and confirm its accounting period.
Map source columns to AFAS accounts and dimensions.
Enter or import the journal details.
Compare ledger totals and line counts with the source and resolve rejected lines.
drudgery: Checking whether an import was already processed
today.time_sinks: Changing file layouts, missing dimensions and unclear recovery after partially rejected imports.

lenses.faster: Replace copying with a controlled source-to-AFAS mapping and automatic control totals. Remove transfers that duplicate entries already integrated within AFAS.
lenses.autonomous: Approval of a supported journal starts validation and import. Schema changes and rejected records stop the workflow for review.
lenses.ambitious: Make every imported line traceable to its source and approval, with completeness checks available throughout the month.
lenses.joy: Remove column shuffling and import babysitting. Keep investigation of genuine source errors.
lenses.options: Preview the mapped journal and rejection report before execution. Compare approved mapping versions when a source format changes.
lenses.altitude: Own journal interfaces, completeness controls and recovery procedures.
reach: Support the Accountant's recurring journal imports.
Help the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst maintain finance-facing data handoffs.

tasks.human_edge: Identifying when a source change alters the accounting meaning rather than merely the file layout.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved structured journals can be mapped, validated and transferred with explicit rules, unique identifiers and reconciliation controls.

in_practice.trigger: A journal with recorded approval is placed in the designated intake location.
steps: Check file schema, approval, batch identifier and accounting period.
Map fields using a versioned configuration and validate all lines.
Submit the validated batch through a supported AFAS import or connector.
Retrieve acceptance results and reconcile line counts, debits and credits.
Hold failed batches for controlled recovery and archive the source and posting references.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves journal content and mapping changes. Bookkeepers handle rejected batches; the workflow cannot create its own approval or reopen closed periods.
data_needed: Unique source identifiers and control totals
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS import and batch references plus a restricted transfer register linking source files, approvals, mapping versions and reconciliation results.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit offers import and connector mechanisms; supported objects and permissions must be checked for this environment.
Versioned mappings, duplicate protection and source-to-ledger control totals are standard integration techniques.

risks: A retry may duplicate accepted lines unless partial failures are handled explicitly.
A changed source format can silently move values into the wrong fields.
An automated import can post into the wrong company or period.
The task may already be handled by AFAS integration, making the estimated saving unavailable.
research_questions: Which journals are genuinely transferred manually rather than already integrated in AFAS?
Which supported import routes provide reliable line-level acceptance results?
Can source identifiers prevent duplicates after timeouts and partial failures?
Will control totals detect missing, duplicated and incorrectly mapped lines before the batch is considered complete?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, customer and supplier records, and resolve differences before close.

today.trigger: A bank statement, supplier statement or reconciliation deadline arrives.
steps: Collect bank transactions, open items and relevant statements.
Match records by reference, amount, date and counterparty.
Investigate missing, duplicated, split or incorrectly allocated items.
Record approved corrections and report unresolved differences.
today.time_sinks: Combined payments, credits, timing differences and repeated requests for missing remittance information.

lenses.faster: Match exact references and supported payment combinations automatically. Assemble the evidence for remaining differences in one work queue.
lenses.autonomous: Each new statement starts reconciliation and updates unresolved items. Only matches satisfying approved rules clear automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile daily across all three sites and identify recurring causes before they delay close or collections.
lenses.joy: Remove line-by-line searching and repeated list maintenance. Keep the detective work that resolves unusual payments and disputes.
lenses.options: Show plausible match combinations and their residual differences. Keep uncertain alternatives open until evidence supports one.
lenses.altitude: Manage reconciliation coverage, aged exceptions and the source problems that create differences.
reach: Prepare cash allocation exceptions for the Credit and Collections Officer.
Provide the Controller with reconciled balances and a close-ready exception list.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a harmless timing difference from a dispute, fraud indicator or accounting error.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow can gather records, propose matches and assemble discrepancy evidence, while a person approves ambiguous allocations and accounting corrections.

in_practice.trigger: A new bank or counterparty statement is available.
steps: Import records and verify statement completeness against opening and closing balances.
Run approved exact and composite matching rules.
Assemble source-backed explanations and candidate matches for unresolved items.
Clear eligible matches and route ambiguous allocations or corrections for approval.
Update the exception register with owner, age and resolution evidence.
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeepers approve ambiguous matches. Write-offs, unusual journals and material corrections follow Finance approval limits; bank transactions are never initiated by reconciliation.
data_needed: Remittance advice, credits and counterparty statements
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS reconciliation references and a restricted exception register containing match evidence, approvals, corrections and ageing.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports bank transaction processing and matching against financial records.
Combining deterministic matching with evidence-backed exception preparation is plausible; performance depends on reference quality and payment complexity.

risks: An incorrect automatic match can conceal a real outstanding balance.
Matching individual lines does not prove statement completeness.
Small write-offs can accumulate into material leakage if tolerances are poorly designed.
Automated correspondence could disclose financial data or make unintended commitments; outbound messages need explicit workflow authorisation.
research_questions: What share of records matches exactly, and what share requires split or combined matches?
Can bank and ledger extracts provide complete, timely records with stable identifiers?
How often are existing matches reversed, and can the pilot reduce that error rate?
Which differences actually delay close, and who has authority to resolve them?

tasks.short: Prepare checked payroll inputs and reconcile payroll totals for the Payroll Specialist.

today.trigger: The payroll cutoff approaches or an approved correction is received.
steps: Collect approved hours, overtime, allowances and payroll corrections.
Check completeness, dates, duplicates and the relevant CAO or agreement.
Prepare the input batch and send discrepancies to the responsible owner.
Hand the checked information to the Payroll Specialist and reconcile approved payroll totals to Finance.
today.time_sinks: Late site submissions, effective-date changes and uncertainty over which allowance rules apply.

lenses.faster: Validate approved inputs against employee, period and allowance rules before the cutoff. Generate a single discrepancy list and payroll-to-ledger reconciliation.
lenses.autonomous: Submission or amendment of an approved input starts validation. The system prepares a batch and highlights changes for Payroll Specialist approval.
lenses.ambitious: Check completeness earlier for every site and explain payroll cost movements before the forecast is updated.
lenses.joy: Remove reformatting and repeated chasing. Keep resolving unusual cases with payroll and site managers.
lenses.options: Show the effect of an approved correction in the current or next payroll period where policy permits. The Payroll Specialist selects the treatment.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality and timeliness of finance-facing payroll inputs and reconciliations.
reach: Support the Payroll Specialist with validation and reconciliation.
Provide FP&A with approved payroll cost movements by site.

tasks.human_edge: Handling pay-sensitive exceptions carefully and recognising when CAO interpretation or employee circumstances require specialist judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources and approvals must be assembled, but calculations should use approved deterministic payroll rules and the Payroll Specialist must approve the batch.

in_practice.trigger: An approved payroll input arrives or the payroll preparation window opens.
steps: Read only the approved employee, period, hours and allowance fields needed for preparation.
Validate completeness, duplicates, effective dates and applicable CAO rule references.
Prepare an input batch and a source-linked exception and change report.
Submit the batch to the Payroll Specialist for review before payroll processing.
After approval, reconcile payroll accounting totals and route any difference for resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: The Payroll Specialist approves inputs and payroll processing; authorised Finance staff separately approve payment. HR and payroll retain responsibility for CAO interpretation and employee cases.
data_needed: Employee payroll identifiers and applicable agreement
Effective-dated CAO rules approved by payroll
Approved payroll results and ledger mapping
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted AFAS payroll audit records and a payroll validation register accessible only to authorised payroll and finance staff.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit provides payroll functionality alongside financial accounting.
Automating input validation and reconciliation is plausible, but the bookkeeper's actual payroll responsibilities and applicable rule coverage are unconfirmed.

risks: Wrong CAO selection or effective dates can cause incorrect pay across many employees.
Agency workers' approved hours and invoices must remain separate from Noordhaven employee payroll.
AVG/GDPR requires data minimisation and restricted access; medical details are unnecessary for this workflow.
HR retains Wet verbetering poortwachter case responsibilities; the workflow must use approved payroll effects rather than infer absence decisions.
Assess any OR consent requirement for changes to staff data or monitoring arrangements. Reassess EU AI Act obligations if scope expands into employment decisions.
research_questions: Which payroll preparation and reconciliation steps do bookkeepers perform today, and which belong solely to the Payroll Specialist?
Where do approved shift hours and allowance inputs originate, and can their approval status be read reliably?
Can every relevant CAO rule be represented with an approved effective date and clear exception handling?
Can a parallel run reproduce approved payroll inputs and accounting totals without exposing unnecessary employee data?

tasks.short: Prepare customer invoices and statements from approved services, rates and account balances.

today.trigger: A billing date arrives or completed services are approved for invoicing.
steps: Collect approved transport or warehouse service details and customer rates.
Calculate charges, surcharges and VAT under the agreed terms.
Prepare and check the invoice or account statement.
Issue the approved document and record it in AFAS.
drudgery: Looking up rates and customer references
today.time_sinks: Missing service approval, disputed quantities, changing surcharges and customer-specific invoice requirements.

lenses.faster: Calculate invoices from approved service records and effective rates. Populate customer references and supporting details without rekeying.
lenses.autonomous: Approved service completion or a billing schedule triggers validation and invoicing under agreed release rules.
lenses.ambitious: Check every approved service for billing completeness and identify unbilled work before month-end.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive invoice assembly. Keep resolving contract ambiguities and preventing customer disputes.
lenses.options: Preview permitted billing groupings, such as per shipment or monthly consolidated invoices. Follow the customer's agreed format when issuing.
lenses.altitude: Own billing completeness, rate quality and first-time invoice acceptance.
reach: Give the Credit and Collections Officer accurate statements and invoice evidence.
Help FP&A identify unbilled approved services and recurring revenue leakage.

tasks.human_edge: Resolving contract interpretation, disputed service delivery and customer relationships when the records do not tell the whole story.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved service quantities, effective rate tables, tax rules and invoice templates support deterministic billing. The source of service records must first be established.

in_practice.trigger: An approved service record becomes billable or a recurring billing date is reached.
steps: Read approved services, customer terms, billing references and effective rates.
Calculate charges and VAT, then check for missing data and duplicate billing.
Create the invoice or statement and validate mandatory fields and control totals.
Release routine documents under approved rules and hold exceptions for review.
Record delivery status and reconcile billed services to the approved source population.
in_practice.human_gate: Finance approves rate tables and routine release rules. Bookkeepers review exceptions; disputed charges, unusual tax treatments and credit notes follow designated approvals.
data_needed: Approved transport and warehouse service records
Customer contracts and effective rate tables
Customer identifiers, invoice references and delivery addresses
Prior invoice lines and service identifiers
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice history plus a billing register linking service records, rate versions, approvals and document delivery results.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports sales invoicing and accounts receivable.
Rule-based billing from approved services is plausible; no transport or warehouse operational system or billing feed was specified.

risks: Incomplete service records can produce faster invoices while leaving revenue unbilled.
Incorrect effective dates or surcharge rules can generate systematic customer disputes.
International transport and other cross-border services may require specialist VAT treatment.
Issuing an invoice twice or sending it to the wrong recipient creates financial and privacy problems.
research_questions: Where are approved transport and warehouse services recorded, and are stable service identifiers available?
What proportion of contracts can be represented by explicit, effective-dated rates and surcharge rules?
Which customer references or supporting documents most often cause invoice rejection?
Can a pilot prove both invoice accuracy and completeness from service approval through successful delivery?

tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and expense reports with the right evidence, coding and approvals.

today.trigger: A site requests a purchase or an employee submits business expenses.
steps: Collect the request, quotation or receipts and business purpose.
Check supplier details, policy requirements and completeness.
Prepare the purchase order or expense report with proposed coding.
Obtain approval and record the approved document in the designated finance process.
today.time_sinks: Incomplete submissions, unclear budget ownership and different document formats across sites.

lenses.faster: Extract receipt and quotation details into a standard form and check required fields immediately. Route the complete draft to the correct approver.
lenses.autonomous: Submission starts duplicate and policy checks, draft preparation and approval routing. Approved documents proceed through the supported finance workflow.
lenses.ambitious: Make committed spending visible by site before invoices arrive and identify recurring policy exceptions early.
lenses.joy: Remove receipt transcription and repeated requests for missing information. Keep helping colleagues submit legitimate expenses correctly.
lenses.options: Show supported coding choices or permitted purchasing alternatives where useful. Budget owners decide what to buy and whether an exception is justified.
lenses.altitude: Own submission quality, approval routing and the causes of purchasing and expense rework.
reach: Support procurement with complete purchase requests and commitment records.
Provide the Controller with approved open commitments and expense liabilities.

tasks.human_edge: Judging business purpose, fairness and unusual circumstances without treating a policy flag as proof of misconduct.
tasks.pattern_why: The workflow assembles varied evidence, prepares documents and routes approvals. A person authorises spending or reimbursement before the result takes effect.

in_practice.trigger: A purchase request or expense claim enters the designated intake form.
steps: Capture required fields and extract receipt or quotation details with document references.
Check arithmetic, duplicates, supplier status and the applicable policy version.
Prepare the order or expense draft with proposed coding and identified exceptions.
Route it to the budget owner or designated approver.
After approval, create the supported AFAS record or controlled export and retain the evidence.
in_practice.human_gate: The budget owner approves purchases and authorised managers approve expenses. Requesters cannot approve their own claims; supplier onboarding and payment release remain separately controlled.
systems: Proposed request and expense intake workflow
data_needed: Requests, quotations, receipts and business purpose
Chart of accounts, VAT guidance and existing claims
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted document and approval records in SharePoint, linked to AFAS references and a workflow history of checks, decisions and policy versions.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Power Automate supports approval workflows that can route requests to human approvers.
Receipt extraction, policy checks and controlled AFAS handoff are plausible, but require confirmation of licensing, modules and integration support.

risks: A convincing receipt may still be duplicated, altered or unrelated to business activity.
An outdated approval matrix can bypass budget ownership or separation of duties.
Expense receipts can reveal personal information beyond what Finance needs.
A policy-checking tool must not become an unreviewed employee misconduct or performance scoring system.
research_questions: Which AFAS modules and workflows currently handle purchasing and employee expenses?
Are approval limits and budget ownership current and consistent across the three sites?
How many submissions are delayed by missing information versus manager approval time?
Can the pilot reduce preparation time while maintaining evidence quality, correct approvals and privacy controls?

role.altitude: Become the owner of reliable transaction flow across payables and receivables: maintain rules, resolve exceptions and deliver reconciled records early enough for a trusted close and forecast.
reach: Prepare source-backed accrual and prepayment candidates for the Accountant.
Maintain reconciliation evidence and aged exceptions for the Controller.
Support the Credit and Collections Officer with cash allocation, statements and dispute evidence.
Give FP&A reliable site coding, approved commitments and unbilled-service information.
Support the Payroll Specialist with approved input validation and payroll-to-ledger reconciliation.
Help procurement address recurring supplier invoice and rate problems.
role.ceiling_note: Current workflows are inferred from the supplied systems and need validation. The eight tasks total 411.9 supplied hours per FTE annually, about 25.7% of the role; their work may overlap, so savings must not be added without observation. Time savings and end-to-end speedups are planning hypotheses, not measured outcomes, and assume the required data and approvals are available. Existing AFAS automation may already capture much of the opportunity. Missing operational feeds, external response times, approval duties and accounting judgement limit further autonomy. Payroll release, payment approval, material write-offs and accounting policy remain with authorised specialists.
skills_to_grow: AFAS configuration, supported imports and connector controls
Reconciliation design, duplicate prevention and recovery from failed batches
Supplier, customer, rate and coding master data management
Dutch VAT fundamentals and recognising cases needing specialist advice
Reading CAO payroll inputs without taking over Payroll Specialist responsibilities
Testing document extraction and measuring incorrect matches and coding suggestions
AVG/GDPR data minimisation, access control and retention
Recognising when staff data changes need OR involvement or expanded AI use needs EU AI Act assessment
Explaining exceptions and their cash, close and forecast effects
role.ambitious_version: Run a daily control process across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo that accounts for incoming invoices, approved commitments, billable services and cash movements. The three bookkeepers spend more time fixing causes of exceptions and preparing reliable close evidence, while Finance tracks days to close, first-pass invoice processing, allocation delays, DSO, forecast accuracy and audit adjustments. Pilot complete flows first, measuring actual hours, errors and waiting time before assigning released capacity to adjacent work.
